text:
alex: Heads-up — I put together a brief proposal to add a 'compact' exporter mode + per-service TTL overrides to the trace pipeline. Goal: cut cold storage egress and speed common queries without touching hot-store SLA. Sketch below.

alex: compact mode = strip non-essential attribute blobs, collapse large baggage into pointers, and write a lightweight index for 90d hot window, then lifecycle to cold with minimal index. Default pipeline TTL stays 90d but services can opt into 7/30/180d.

alex: example OTEL exporter config we tried locally:```yaml
exporters:
  redwood_compact:
    mode: compact
    drop_attributes: [debug.stack, user_agent.full, raw_body]
    index_ttl_days: 90
    service_ttl_overrides:
      billing-service: 180
      ai-inference: 30
      signup: 7
```

maria: quick Q — how do we handle rehydration when someone needs full spans for a debug session? Do we keep a blob store with original payloads for N days, or re-run sampling to reconstruct? :thinking:

alex: plan A is to keep full raw payloads in cold blob store (S3) for 365d for legal/audit, but they won't be indexed. Rehydration job will pull blob and re-ingest to the hot index on demand (on a per-trace ticket) — expect ~30s extra latency for queries that trigger rehydrate.

sasha: we should be careful: re-ingesting changes trace ids ordering & could confuse timeline-based dashboards. Recommend rehydrate writes a rehydration marker and preserves original trace id + a secondary field so dashboards can hide rehydrated traces by default.

tomas: main concern is query performance for artists/frontline support — cold lookups with partial index is fine, but we need a fast path for trace search by request_id across 30d. Can compact index keep request_id + span timestamps?

alex: yes, compact index keeps these fields: trace_id, request_id, service, root_span_name, start_ts, duration, error_flag — enough for fast search across the hot window. Full span payloads live in cold.

june: compliance/legal: if retention_override extends beyond default (e.g., billing-service 180d), we need a per-customer hold API to pin traces for litigation. Also audit logs for each rehydrate.

alex: agreed — adding an 'audit.rehydrate_by' and 'retention.hold' tag and exposing an admin API for holds. We'll need KMS integration per private deployment.

infra-bot: quick estimate: switching low-cardinality services to compact mode could cut cold S3 bytes by ~45% and index size by ~30% based on sampling job last week.

maria: implementation details — where do TTL overrides live? In exporter config, or central routing policy? If in exporter, infra teams need to redeploy for changes. If central, runtime can change without deploy.

alex: thinking central config (console) + per-service default in exporter for fail-open. Console exposes a per-service TTL override and an audit history so we can change without code deploys. Exporter reads a cached policy with a 5m refresh.

sasha: UX for console — show cost delta when you change TTL, and a quick query to preview how many traces get impacted. Also warn when lowering TTL for services with active SLOs around observability.

tomas: rollout plan? Recommend feature-flag rollout: start with beta on non-prod namespaces, then gradual opt-in for low-cardinality services. Need migration/backfill script for services that want historic compaction applied retroactively.

alex: yep — proposed steps: 1) build compact write path + index, 2) UI for TTL overrides + cost estimate, 3) staged rollout to staging, 4) run backfill tool for opt-ins, 5) monitor query latencies and 95th percentile error surface.

june: reminder — coordinate with security before we enable rehydrate in private deployments (HSM/KMS). Also make sure legal gets a heads-up for any 365d cold retention policy.

maria: testing checklist: unit tests for compaction rules, integration tests that rehydrate end-to-end, and UX smoke test for cost calc. Add perf test for trace search baseline.

sasha: +1. Can we add a small telemetry tag to traces written in compact mode so we can measure coverage and failures?

alex: yes — add attribute 'rw.pipeline.compact_mode=true' and 'rw.compact.version=1'.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: telemetry/compact-writer -> staging at 2026-03-24T03:00Z (canary 10%).

tomas: :thumbsup: I'll schedule a short runbook for on-call for the canary window.

alex: thanks all. Action items: I will PR the compact writer RFC, sasha will prototype console cost calc, june will loop in legal/security, maria will own tests, tomas will schedule canary. Backfill tooling follow-up next week.

sasha: sounds good — also adding a note to the docs about how rehydration affects timelines and dashboards.

alex: filing RFC today.
